newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S., China mark 25th year of ping-pong diplomacy.
newsitem.headline: U.S., China mark 25th year of ping-pong diplomacy.

text.p: They played ping-pong at the United Nations on Thursday to celebrate an historic landmark in diplomacy.
The occasion was the 25th anniversary of the 1971-72 exchange of visits by Chinese and United States table tennis teams that helped dissolve years of hostility between their two countries.
On hand for the occasion were former U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger, who used ping-pong diplomacy to fashion a new opening to Beijing, and China's current U.N. ambassador, Qin Huasun.
Present-day players and some veterans of the original teams demonstrated their skills, volleying across a table set up in the cavernous U.N. delegates' lounge.
A huge tapesty of China's Great Wall, a gift from Beijing that has long decorated the lounge, served as a perfect backdrop for the reception, speechmaking and exhibition matches.
"Every once in a while something happens in diplomacy which transcends the drafting of cables and the formal messages that are sent," Kissinger said.

"And by adding a human dimension to what seemed to be a very frozen situation, the table tennis team really made a tremendous contribution," he said, detailing how the way was opened for President Richard Nixon to visit China in 1972.
Nixon's daughter, Tricia, and her husband, Edward Cox, were in the audience.
"And now we are in a new world, and conditions have changed," Kissinger said.

When Chinese President Jiang Zemin visits the United States this autumn, "we have an opportunity, and I would say almost an obligation, to try to set a pattern that will last us for another few decades, which is adapted to the new conditions," he added.

Kissinger, alluding to President Bill Clinton, said those like himself who served in U.S. Republican administrations "will gladly support a Democratic president if he continues on the road that was charted then, adapting it to the conditions of the present period."

Qin, China's U.N. envoy, hinting at the frequent ups and downs in Sino-U.S. relations, said: "Today, while we commemorate the 25th anniversary of ping-pong diplomacy, it is all the more necessary to cherish and protect this hard-won friendship."

Also needed were "more people of insight ... to work together to enhance understanding between the two peoples and to promote the establishment of 21st century-oriented, long-term, stable and healthy relations between the two countries."
The event was organised by the National Committee on United States-China Relations, China's U.N. mission and the U.N. Recreation Council.
